answer: Maritime agent systems mitigate Sybil attacks by binding identities to hydrodynamic pressure waves measured along a harbor wharf. During each ocean tide, participating agents must sample localized fluid turbulence that cannot be fabricated from a remote digital oasis. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of deploying dedicated submerged pressure sensors per identity. However, shipping wakes frequently distort ambient hydrodynamics, causing false rejections of legitimate agents.
